surviving.title: Ring (N > 1): minimal period / wave number is not established; N*tau is only shown to be a period
surviving.claim: For N > 1 the program shows only that the fixed point x* satisfies phi(tau, x*) = Q x*, where (Qx)_k = x_{k+1}. So x_j(t) = phi(t + j tau), and N tau is a period. It does not exclude a k-pulse rotating wave (k >= 2) with minimal period N tau/k. Every check in verify.cpp also passes for such a solution: a fixed point of g, first upward crossing of V_{N-1} at tau, V_{N-1}(0) < s on the box. So "a rotating wave of period N times the section time" holds only in the sense "N tau is a period". Wave number one (a single reentrant wave), which is the scientific claim, is unproved. Nonsynchrony is established: the guard at line 163 forces V_{N-1} < s = V_0 on all of Y, which excludes the synchronous orbit. It is not recorded in the JSON or the README.
surviving.evidence: Take N = 8 and a 3-pulse wave: phi_cell has period 8tau/3 and x_j(t) = phi(t + j tau). Cell 7 crosses upward at t = -7tau + i(8tau/3); the crossings nearest 0 are -5tau/3 and tau. So the first upward crossing after 0 is at tau, exactly what CAPD computes for P. phi(tau, x) = Qx holds, so g(x) = x. V_7(0) = phi(5tau/3), phase 5/8 after the upstroke, which is below s for a normal AP shape, so the line 163 guard passes too. A 2-wave (period 4tau) passes in the same way. Nothing in run<N>() counts upward crossings of the other cells on (0, tau), and nothing compares cells at t = 0. Both runs use the same pm/section (lines 105-106, 62-63), whose only semantics are "first upward crossing of V_{N-1}".
surviving.fix: Add a rigorous check that phi has exactly one upward crossing of s in [0, N tau). Then the minimal period of phi, which is the minimal period of the ring orbit, is N tau, since a k-wave has k such crossings. phi on [j tau, (j+1) tau) is cell j on [0, tau). So integrate the C0 or C1 box enclosure step by step up to the section crossing. On every step enclosure, for each cell j = 1..N-2 (and for cell 0 after it leaves s), require either that V_j - s excludes 0 or that f_{V_j} < 0 (downward crossings only). Until that check exists, state the result as "N tau is a period, the orbit is not synchronous", and record the nonsynchrony guard in the JSON.

verdicts.why:
The finding holds, and nothing in verify.cpp rules out the failure it describes.

1. The ring field really is Z_N-equivariant. In model/tp06_capd.hpp, ringField couples each cell to its neighbours as c*(V_{k-1} - 2V_k + V_{k+1}), indices mod N. So a fixed point x* of g (verify.cpp lines 5-6, 153-154, 169-178: g(x)_j = P(x)_{j-1}) gives phi(tau, x*) = Q x* with (Qx)_k = x_{k+1}. Then x_j(t) = x_0(t + j tau), and N tau is a period. Nothing more is established.

2. A k-wave passes every check. Take a solution x_j(t) = phi(t + j k Tc/N), where phi is a cell oscillation of minimal period Tc. For the self-oscillating cells used here (near the Hopf point), such phase-locked k-waves are ordinary solutions of a ring of identical oscillators.
   - V_{N-1}(t) = phi(t - k Tc/N mod Tc). For 1 <= k < N, its first upward crossing of s after t = 0 is at tau = k Tc/N. That is exactly what pm with MinusPlus on {V_{N-1} = s} returns (lines 62-63, 105-106).
   - phi(tau, x) = Q x holds, so g(x) = x.
   - The only shape guard is line 163: V_{N-1}(0) < s on the box. Here V_{N-1}(0) = phi at phase 1 - k/N, which is below s for small k with a normal waveform, so the guard passes.
   - The contraction checks (lines 228-282) concern only the local fixed point and its derivative. They pass for any hyperbolic stable fixed point, whatever its wave number.
   - The program then prints "period" = N*T (lines 299, 302) = k*Tc. That is a period, but k times the minimal period, and the wave number is unproved.

3. Nothing pins the wave number:
   - The centre xhat comes from the untrusted orbit_newton.cpp. Its intended guess is x_j = phi(jT/N) (lines 11-12), but verify.cpp never checks the spatial profile of xhat or of the box.
   - There is no count of upward crossings of other cells on (0, tau).
   - There is no comparison between cells at t = 0 beyond the end-cell guard.

4. The finding's arithmetic is correct. For N = 8 and a 3-wave, cell 7 crosses at t = tau(8i/3 - 7); the first positive value is tau (i = 3), and the previous one is -5tau/3. V_7(0) sits at phase 5/8.

5. Nonsynchrony is established as the finding says: line 163 encloses all of Y and forces V_{N-1} < s = V_0, which excludes the synchronous orbit.

The stability conclusion is unaffected, since the multipliers over the minimal period are k-th roots of those over N tau. So this cannot produce a false VERIFIED on the contraction claim. What it does is leave README:46-47 ("a rotating wave of period N times the section time") and README:58 / verify.cpp:18-19 ("the period ... N T") supported only as "N tau is a period". Neither minimal period nor wave number one is proved.

Since no N > 1 run exists yet (README: "Everything else: not started"), medium is the right severity: a check or a qualified statement is needed before any ring result is claimed.

I could not refute this finding, and it holds as stated.

**What the program proves for N > 1.** A fixed point of g means x_j = P(x)_{j-1}. The ring field (model/tp06_capd.hpp:174-187) is cyclically symmetric, so this gives y(t+tau) = Q y(t) and y_j(t) = y_0(t + j tau). That makes N tau a period. It does not make N tau the minimal period.

**Other waves pass every check.** Take a twisted wave with wave number m, where the cell orbit has period T_c and the delay is tau = m T_c / N:
- For 1 <= m <= N-1, tau lies in (0, T_c).
- V_{N-1}(t) = phi_V(t - tau), so its first upward crossing after 0 is at tau. That is exactly what the MinusPlus Poincare map at verify.cpp:105-106 and 62-63 finds.
- The only structural guard, at verify.cpp:163, asks for V_{N-1}(0) = phi_V(-tau) < s. It holds whenever phase -m/N falls in the part of the cycle below s.

For the near-Hopf plateau oscillation here (section time about 53.6 ms, roughly sinusoidal), that means about m < N/2. So for N = 8, the m = 2 and m = 3 twisted states pass. The guard does exclude the synchronous state and the reverse-direction 1-wave (m = N-1, which sits just after its upward crossing).

**Nothing else in run<N>() looks at it.** The program never examines the crossings of the other cells on (0, tau), never compares cells to each other, and never inspects the trajectory enclosure. It reports "period" = N*T (line 299) without justification. The contraction argument certifies a unique fixed point near the untrusted xhat. It says nothing about which wave number that fixed point has. The m >= 2 states are also not exotic: each cell is an autonomous oscillator and the coupling is weak (c = N^2 D = 1e-3 per ms for N = 8). Twisted states with several values of m plausibly coexist, and some may be stable. So the untrusted orbit_newton.cpp could converge to one of them, and verify.cpp would still print VERIFIED with "period N T".

**Contrast with N = 1.** For N = 1 the first-return argument does force T to be the minimal period. That argument does not carry over to the ring.

**The strongest defence fails.** One could read "period" as "a period", and the README never says "wave number one" literally. But README line 47 ("a rotating wave of period N times the section time"), the comment at verify.cpp:19 and the JSON "period" field would all be read as the minimal period of a single reentrant wave. That claim is unsupported.

**Fix.** The proposed fix is sound. Because x_j(t) = phi(t + j tau), the cells' trajectories over [0, tau] cover phi over [0, N tau]. A rigorous count of the upward crossings of s along the box enclosure would settle the wave number. Medium is the right severity: the program would not print VERIFIED for a false fixed-point or stability claim, but the README's "period N times the section time" needs a missing check or a weaker wording.

surviving.title: N > 1: the step from eigenvalues of Dg to Floquet multipliers and orbital stability is asserted without its (equivariance) argument
surviving.claim: For a ring, g = Q^{-1} P is not a first-return map of the orbit. Its eigenvalues are not the Floquet multipliers of the period-N tau orbit; those multipliers are their N-th powers. The README's statement "every nontrivial Floquet multiplier has modulus at most q" and the stability conclusion are both correct, but they rest on the equivariance f(Qx) = Q f(x), which neither file states or argues. A manuscript needs that derivation. The sharp bound is q^N, not q.
surviving.evidence: Let h(x) = Q^{-1} phi(tau*, x) at fixed tau*. Use e_END^T Q = e_0^T and f(Qx) = Q f(x); the second holds for the coded ring field, tp06_capd.hpp:179-185 (identical cells, symmetric coupling, per-cell scaling). Then Dg_full = Q^{-1}(I - f(Px*) e_END^T / f_END(Px*)) Dphi = Pi0 Dh, with Pi0 = I - f(x*) e_0^T / f_0(x*). Since Dh f(x*) = f(x*), the eigenvalues of Dg on TS0 are those of Dh with one 1 removed. Also phi(N tau*, .) = h^N, so the monodromy is Dh^N and the multipliers are lambda^N, |lambda^N| <= q^N < 1. I checked this algebra against the code: shiftBackRows = Pshift*DP (lines 154, 207), and dropping row/column 0 (lines 208-209) gives Dg restricted to TS0 in the free coordinates.
surviving.fix: Write this derivation in the README and the manuscript: equivariance, Dg|TS0 is the quotient of Dh modulo f, monodromy = Dh^N. Then state that the nontrivial multipliers of the period-N tau orbit are lambda^N, with modulus <= q^N.

surviving.title: CAPD crossSectionInOneStep trims the crossing bound with the previous Newton iterate's endpoints, while monotonicity is checked only on the current iterate
surviving.location: CAPD 6.1.0 include/capd/poincare/PoincareMap_templateMembers.h:260-273 (used by verify.cpp:205 for Px and by verify.cpp:69/187 via PoincareMap_templateOperator.h:62-119 for G(0))
surviving.claim: In each Newton iteration CAPD does three things: bound = c(newReturnTime); vfOnBound = f(c(newReturnTime)); then bound_j is intersected with hull(c(old.left)_j, c(old.right)_j). That hull is valid only if x_j is monotone on the whole old interval. The f_j check that guards it covers only the new interval, and the earlier check over the old interval has already been overwritten. On the normal exit (old == new, the break at line 270) the two coincide and the code is sound. If the loop runs all 10 iterations without reaching equality, the last intersection can drop true values. The case is a component with a turning point in new9 \ new10, where the true values at t in new10 lie outside hull(x_j(new9.left), x_j(new9.right)) and bound_j only partly overlaps that hull. Px feeds f(Px) in computeDP. In the affine operator, bound feeds both the second-order term and the final intersection with A(bound - c). A dropped value would therefore corrupt DG or G(0).
surviving.evidence: Lines 260-268: `bound = c(newReturnTime); vfOnBound = f(..., bound); L = c(oneStepReturnTime.left()); R = c(oneStepReturnTime.right()); if(!vfOnBound[j].contains(0)) intersection(bound[j], intervalHull(L[j],R[j]), bound[j]);` At this point oneStepReturnTime still holds the previous iterate. My tests: a single-iteration turning-point case was enclosed correctly. A 4800-case scan with slowly contracting Newton (review/hullscan.cpp) found no missed enclosure. Reaching the gap needs a non-converged 10th iteration and a turning point inside a tiny window, so in practice it is very unlikely. It is still a gap in the trusted base, not a proof.
surviving.fix: Note it in the trust-boundary section. Optionally report it upstream. To harden verify.cpp, check after each Poincare call that the crossing-time interval converged (re-run with a smaller step if not), or recompute the image without CAPD's monotone-hull trimming as a cross-check.

surviving.title: CAPD crossSectionInOneStep can tighten the crossing-point bound using the wrong window when its Newton loop stops at the 10-iteration cap
surviving.location: capd/poincare/PoincareMap_templateMembers.h:221-274 (CAPD 6.1.0 install). verify.cpp reads this bound at line 66 (affine operator, PoincareMap_templateOperator.h:92 and :119) and at lines 196-197 (Px = bound, used as fieldOnPx in computeDP).
surviving.claim: Inside the Newton loop, CAPD sets bound = c(newReturnTime) and checks monotonicity of each coordinate j on that set (vfOnBound). It then intersects bound[j] with hull(c(oneStepReturnTime.left())[j], c(oneStepReturnTime.right())[j]), which are the endpoints of the previous, wider window. When the loop ends with old == new (the break), the two windows are the same and the step is correct. When the loop ends because i reaches 10 with old != new, the last intersection survives with mismatched endpoints. If coordinate j turns around inside old minus new while f_j over c(new) still excludes 0, the true x_j(t*) can lie outside that hull. In that case Px, and A(P(x)-c), no longer enclose the true values, and the program could still print VERIFIED. verify.cpp has no way to detect this.
surviving.evidence: Code at lines 260-274: `bound = c(newReturnTime); vfOnBound = f(..., bound); L = c(oneStepReturnTime.left()); R = c(oneStepReturnTime.right()); if(!vfOnBound[j].contains(0)) intersection(bound[j], intervalHull(L[j],R[j]), bound[j]); if(oneStepReturnTime == newReturnTime) break; oneStepReturnTime = newReturnTime;`. Counter-model in one coordinate: x_j(t) = (t-tau)^2 with old = [0,1], new = [0.4,0.6], tau = 0.3, and the crossing at t* = 0.5. f_j > 0 on new, so the intersection is applied. The hull is [0.09, 0.49], and it excludes the true value 0.04. The capped exit does happen in CAPD 6.1.0: an instrumented copy of the header (scratchpad/review/capdapi/inc, test newton10.cpp, x'=p, p in [1,1.0001], fixed step 2) printed `oneStep Newton hit cap: old=[0, 9.9990000999917268e-05] new=[0, 9.9990000999916943e-05]`. In every capped exit observed, the last cut is a few ulps, so a wrong exclusion would need f_j's enclosure over c(new) to exclude 0 while x_j turns within that sliver. For the cardiac runs this is practically impossible, but nothing in the code rules it out.
surviving.fix: Either use a patched local copy of this function (take L and R at newReturnTime's endpoints, or skip the per-coordinate tightening when the loop did not converge), or state this CAPD behaviour in the README's trust boundary together with the argument above for why it cannot bite here.

surviving.title: README domain argument names the wrong mechanism, and the MP centre run has an unchecked log that can fail silently
surviving.claim: README says an out-of-domain enclosure 'produces an unbounded interval' through filib's extended mode, so the run 'cannot pass silently'. That is not how this build behaves. capd::interval is filib i_mode_normal; the -DFILIB_EXTENDED from capd-config does not change it. In the double runs, CAPD's filib wrapper throws IntervalError when a log argument has left bound <= 0, when a divisor interval contains 0, or when sqrt gets a negative argument. CAPD's step control catches the error, retries with a smaller step, and rethrows at the minimum step, so those runs do fail loudly. An exp overflow is different: filib's q_exp calls std::terminate, which nothing can catch. exp(5(V+40)) overflows above about 101.9 mV, so a trial enclosure reaching that aborts the process instead of shrinking the step. That is fail-safe but not a retry. The 128-bit centre run uses CAPD's MpInterval instead. Its log has no domain check, and CAPD's MpInterval product turns NaN bounds into [0,0]. So in the MP run, a log argument that is entirely negative continues silently with E_Na (or E_Ca, E_Ks) replaced by 0. A divisor containing 0 still throws in MpInterval. The README argument therefore covers only evaluation boxes that contain a true, positive state. It does not cover evaluation at points that are not true states, such as x0 = mid(X) in the affine Poincare operator or the Lohner centre. With point-sized 128-bit sets this cannot happen in practice, but the 'cannot pass silently' claim is not established for the MP run as written.

Test program (review/t1): 1/[-1,1], log([-1,2]) and log([-2,-1]) all throw IntervalError (a std::runtime_error); exp(800) prints 'filib: q_exp overflow' and calls terminate. MP side: MpInterval.cpp:432-443 computes log as [log(lo) rounded down, log(hi) rounded up], then calls testNaN(res). testNaN (MpInterval_Fun.hpp:34-41) does nothing unless __MPI_TEST_NAN__ is defined, and MpIntervalSettings.h:24 has `//#define __MPI_TEST_NAN__`. surviving.fix: Rewrite README lines 60-62 to describe the real mechanisms: IntervalError thrown and retried, then rethrown, in the double runs, and terminate on exp overflow. Defining __MPI_TEST_NAN__ as it stands will not compile, because MpInterval_Fun.hpp:36 has an unbalanced parenthesis. (b) Pass each log argument through a checked operation in the model, e.g. log(a) = 2*log(sqrt(a)); MpInterval sqrt throws on a negative left bound. (c) Write down the argument that every MP evaluation set contains the true state, including the midpoint evaluations, and cite where CAPD evaluates the enclosure on a superset first.

verdicts.why:
The finding has two parts. The substantive one, that the 128-bit centre run's log "can fail silently", describes a failure that cannot happen. The minor one, that the README names the wrong mechanism, is true but is only a wording error.

1. Confirmed sub-claims. capd::interval is filib i_mode_normal (capd/intervals/lib.h:55). Division by an interval containing 0, and log with a left bound <= 0, throw IntervalError (filib/Interval.h:391, 690). MpInterval log has no domain check: MpInterval.cpp:432-443, and testNaN is compiled out (MpIntervalSettings.h:24). So README line 61 ("produces an unbounded interval") describes the wrong mechanism. The run actually fails by an exception, which reaches main()'s catch and prints NOT VERIFIED, or, on an exp overflow, by terminate before anything is written. Either way the README's conclusion, that the run fails and cannot pass silently, still holds.

2. The silent-NaN path needs an evaluation set whose Na_i or Ca_i is entirely negative. MpInterval division uses the generic Interval_Op.hpp operator/. It throws whenever the divisor's left bound is <= 0 and its right bound is >= 0 (Interval_Op.hpp:441-443). That includes [0, b]. I checked this on the real model: review/refute_dom.cpp evaluates MpIMap ringField<1> and its derivative on boxes with Na_i = [-1, 9], [0, 9], Ca_i = [-1e-5, 2e-4] or [0, 2e-4]. Every case throws "Possible division by zero". Only an entirely negative box passes silently.

In this program, every evaluation set is one of two kinds:
   - (a) A convex box that contains the true state phi(t, xc), whose concentrations are positive. xc is the start point, and its positivity is checked by verify.cpp:158-161, since X = xc + A*r contains xc. Such a box is never entirely negative, so if it reaches 0 the division throws. These boxes are:
     - the hull m_currentSet, on which HighOrderEnclosure evaluates the Taylor and remainder coefficients;
     - enc, which contains phi, which contains the hull;
     - the box in the step-control init (y = x + [0,h] f(x), which contains x);
     - lastEnclosure and c(t) for t inside the step domain, in getCloserToSection, crossSectionInOneStep and checkTransversability;
     - bound and X in the affine operator.
   - (b) A point that lies inside a box of kind (a) evaluated in the same operation:
     - The Lohner centre: C0TripletonSet.hpp move() takes the centre as m_x only if subset(m_x, m_currentSet), and otherwise as the midpoint of m_currentSet. The same encloseC0Map call then evaluates on m_currentSet, so a bad centre aborts the move by the throw.
     - x0 = mid(X) in PoincareMap_templateOperator.h:106: derivative(X) is evaluated first at line 102. If X's Ca_i or Na_i touched 0 that line throws; otherwise mid(X) is positive.

   By induction from the positive start point, no evaluation set can be entirely negative. So the MP log never receives a negative argument, and the README's denominator-first argument does cover the MP run. The finding's own text concedes that the failure cannot occur with point-sized sets. In fact it cannot occur at all with this call pattern.

3. The exp overflow calls terminate, which the finding itself calls fail-safe: verify.cpp writes the JSON only at the end, and the output file is truncated when it is opened.

The only residual issue is the README mechanism wording at lines 60-62: "unbounded interval" should read "IntervalError is thrown and the run reports NOT VERIFIED; an exp overflow aborts the process". This is a documentation error with no effect on rigor, so it is low severity.

I refute the soundness half of the finding but uphold the documentation half, so the severity drops from medium to low.

**Part refuted: the 128-bit centre run cannot pass silently.** It is true that MpInterval log of an argument that is entirely negative returns NaN and that the run then continues (review/refute_dom: with Na_i entirely negative, f evaluates without error). But CAPD never evaluates such a point on its own. Each such point lies inside a box that the same operation also evaluates, and that box contains a true state.

1. **Lohner centre.** C0TripletonSet.hpp:96-103 takes the centre x to be m_x when m_x is inside m_currentSet, and mid(m_currentSet) otherwise, so x always lies in m_currentSet.
   - encloseC0Map (OdeSolver.hpp:118 and OdeSolver.h:251-252) calls computeCoefficientsAtCenter(x) and then computeCoefficients(xx = m_currentSet) in the same call.
   - By induction, m_currentSet contains the true state. The start point xc has positive concentrations: the guard at verify.cpp:205 checks the box X, and X contains xc.
   - So if the centre's Na_i or Ca_i is not positive, the hull's Na_i or Ca_i interval contains 0, and the divisions Na_o/Na_i or Ca_o/Ca_i throw "Possible division by zero". MpInterval division does throw, and the exception derives from std::exception.
   - E_Ks goes negative only when Na_i < -4610, and then Na_i in the hull also contains 0.
   - TimeMap_template.h:63 retries with a smaller step and rethrows at the minimum step; PoincareMap has no catch. The exception reaches main's catch, which prints NOT VERIFIED.
2. **Midpoint in the affine Poincare operator.** At PoincareMap_templateOperator.h:101-106, derivative(t, X) on the hull X runs before f(x0) at x0 = mid(X), and f(X) is evaluated as well. The same argument applies.
3. **Every other evaluation** in PoincareMap_templateMembers.h is on an enclosure (bound or oneStepBound). The step-size choice only reads stored coefficients and does not affect rigour.

I checked this directly (review/ctr_step.cpp, 128 bits, order 30). I took a set whose centre has negative Na_i (and, in a second case, negative Ca_i) and whose hull straddles 0. Both the plain solver step and the full MpIPoincareMap threw "Possible division by zero"; neither passed silently. So no CAPD patch and no check in the model is needed. The finding's own words, "cannot happen in practice", understate this: it cannot happen at all.

**Part upheld: the README describes the wrong mechanism.** README.md lines 60-62 say an out-of-domain enclosure "produces an unbounded interval". In this build it does not.
- In the double runs, filib normal mode (mode=0) throws IntervalError on a divisor containing 0 and on log or sqrt of a nonpositive argument (review/t1, cases 1, 2, 3, 7, 8).
- In the MP run, the divisor throws as described above.
- In the double runs, an exp overflow (exp(5(V+40)) for V above about 101.9 mV) calls std::terminate (t1, case 6). That is fail-safe, but it aborts the process rather than retrying with a smaller step.

The README's conclusion ("the run fails; it cannot pass silently") is correct for every run. Only the stated mechanism is wrong, and the README does not spell out the centre and midpoint argument above. That is a documentation inaccuracy, not a gap that could produce VERIFIED for a false claim. Two small corrections to the finding: README does not mention "filib's extended mode", which the finding attributes to it; and the fix needs only a README rewrite (exceptions, then retry, then rethrow; terminate on exp overflow; centre and midpoint covered by the hull evaluation), not options (a) or (b).

surviving.title: VERIFY_MP_BITS below 53 silently makes the centre enclosure non-rigorous, and the setting is not recorded
surviving.claim: mpBits comes from the environment with no lower bound. Any value > 0 takes the MP path. That calls checkTransversability(theSet, getLastEnclosure()) (:57, :396-412) after every leave step. If V-s on a step's rough enclosure W_k contains 0, f_V over W_k must exclude 0, or the run throws. This rules out the finding's scenario ("box straddles at an endpoint, so points cross upward undetected"):
- Two consecutive steps whose enclosures both meet the section share the true points at their common endpoint. So f_V has the same sign in both, and a down-chain cannot turn straight into an up-chain.
- Any box point x that crossed upward at some t* in (0, t_L] must first pass a V-minimum at t_m < t*, where V < s and f_V = 0. The step j containing t_m therefore has an enclosure W_j strictly below s, or checkTransversability would have thrown.

**The gap that remains.** In C0DoubletonSet::move (C0DoubletonSet.hpp:74-90), m_currentSet is (y+rem+jacPhi*deltaX) intersected with the doubleton form. It is never intersected with the step enclosure `enc`. So CAPD does not guarantee that the endpoint representation lies inside W_j. If it reaches s while W_j is strictly below, the box run's leave phase can carry on through the next upstroke. The box run then resolves a later crossing than the thin MPFR run, while the centre run resolves the first return. G0 and DG would then come from different maps, and the invariance and contraction test could still pass.

This takes a numerical pathology and is very unlikely for a small box. But it is not excluded by the code or by any written argument.

The leave-loop argument above should also be written down to support the N = 1 first-return (minimal period) claim.

Severity stays medium: this is a gap that needs an argument and a check added, not an exploitable path to a false VERIFIED under normal CAPD behaviour.

Whenever the step's rough enclosure enc_k meets the section, f_END over enc_k (dV/dt) must exclude 0, or a PoincareException is thrown. PoincareException derives from std::runtime_error and is caught in main (verify.cpp:375), so the run reports NOT VERIFIED.

A step whose enclosure lies strictly below s never occurs inside the loop.

3. Chain argument. Two consecutive touching steps both contain the true set at their shared endpoint, so their dV/dt signs agree. Now take any trajectory x of either set that goes strictly below s after t0 (V(t0) = s) and first returns to s at t' before the loop exits. Every step whose interior meets (t0, t') contains a value below s. By step 2 each such step is a touching step, and they are consecutive, so they share one sign. The first of them needs dV/dt < 0 (x leaves s downward) and the last needs dV/dt > 0 (x reaches s from below). That is a contradiction. So within the loop, once V < s it stays below s. At exit the true set is strictly below s (H_exit[END] < s). Hence for every x the exit time lies in (tau1(x), tau2(x)). Here tau1(x) is x's first downward crossing; before it V > s, because a touching V = s point in the interior is impossible when dV/dt has one sign. tau2(x) is the next upward hit.

4. After the exit, the first-return loop (line 124, also 3-argument getSign), crossSectionInOneStep and crossSection all check transversality step by step. CAPD's result therefore encloses phi(t*(x), x), where t*(x) is the first hit of s after the exit. That equals tau2(x), the first upward crossing of S0 after t = 0. This time is a property of x's trajectory alone. It does not depend on step sizes, set width, solver order or precision.

So the MPFR centre run and the double C1 box run evaluate the same map g(x) = phi(tau2(x), x) at xc and over the box respectively. For each point the derivative is that of this map (transversal crossing), and T encloses the true first-return time, as the README states. The finding's scenario cannot happen: a box straddling the section at a step endpoint, with box points crossing upward undetected. Straddling only produces touching steps, which carry the one-sign condition on dV/dt. If the set really had a down-then-up excursion during the leave phase, the run would throw, not skip a crossing. `subset(Tc, T)` is therefore not needed for soundness; an intersection test would only be a redundant diagnostic. Both times are already recorded in the JSON (verify.cpp:351).

computeDP gives DP = DPhi + f(Px) dT, with dT from the gradient of the end section {V_{N-1} = s}. That is the right section for N > 1. shiftBackRows = Pshift*DP. Row 0 of DG is DP's row END, which is zero because the image lies on V_{N-1} = s. Column 0 is the transverse direction. So DG[1:,1:] is Dg restricted to TS0 in the free coordinates, and M = At^{-1} DGt At.
The frame A = [[1,0],[0,At]] with r[0] = 0 keeps every point of the box exactly on S0: V_0 = xhat[0] = level, checked at line 110. The level 0.2/0.25 is exact.

This makes T(x) the first upward return for each point. At T_min the orbit is at x* with V' > 0, having been below just before, so T(x*) <= T_min, while T(x*) is a period. Hence T(x*) is the minimal period, and it lies in the box time T. The argument is not written down anywhere, but it holds.

N > 1: a fixed point gives phi(tau, x*) = Q x*. With f(Qx) = Q f(x) for the coded ring field, x_j(t) = phi(t + j tau), and N tau is a period. The stability conclusion from eig(Dg) is correct (see finding 2).

Parameter intervals: both runs use enclosures valid for every g_Ks in the hull (MP and double decimal enclosures), so the conclusions hold for each g_Ks in the interval.
